title: First jobs, Bunk Johnson and the kazoo band
summary: Early jobs with Norman Blaze and Cornbread, a wartime gig with Bunk Johnson, Papa Celestine, the kazoo band and house parties.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: You were going to ask him about the different, want me to ask him about some of the different people that I know that he played with.

Um, yeah, well, Dave, um, you were telling me downstairs, um, about some of the first groups you, you, you worked with. Um, can you say that again? Who, who, who, who were the first people who gave you jobs? And, uh, and you, you.

Well, I played jobs, I played jobs with boys like, uh, well, they were men over me, but I was quite young. They was, uh, like Euleth John. Like I first said, I played jobs with, uh, Norman Blaze, which was a drummer. I mean, he never played a job on Bowman Street before in his life. I'm more than sure, Euleth John either.

Well, I played with those people. I played with Brother Cornbread, and many others. I even played with Bunk Johnson. I played gigs with, you know, many of them old timers way, way back, where they was in the game and then fell out of it.
Tell me when, now how old were you when you played with Bunk? Was this a?
Well, well, well, well, Bunk, this was in, uh, this was a thing right fast, did, uh, I remember, I came in on, I came in on a furlough. It was during wartime with Bunk.

I came in on furlough. Well, he needed piano playing right fast. Well, I was even surprised, because I knew about him, but I knew he hadn't already gotten out the game. Mm-hmm. You know, I didn't even thought he was even working anymore, because I mean, I never did see him fooling around New Orleans. Yeah, I knew he'd come out of a little country town, you know.
Yeah. Do you remember the place?

So I happened to, uh, well, I mean, I played a gig with him, I mean, uh, truthfully, I played a gig with him, in, uh, in Lashville, Lux, Lux, in Louisiana. Oh, yeah. And I, and I, I played a gig with him, in, uh, uh, right up here, around his bridge there, uh, Boutique. Uh-huh. Boutique, Louisiana, I played a gig with him. How many? How many? Playing, you know, those are the things I did with him, two, three things.
How many pieces did he have with him? Well, he had about seven pieces.

I never just stayed with him long, but it's, it was a kick to play with him old-timers like him. I played with Papa Celestine. Yeah. I never was a regular member. Yeah. But I played, you know, like they needed, I guess couldn't get through by now, so I played with those. Yeah. Which, uh, but I tell you people, like I said, that never hit Boydman Street, I played with, like, boys like Eulah Jones. Yeah. Uh, well, she's on Boydman Street now, but I remember during the time this boy, uh, playing drum with us there at the mids on Boydman, uh, Alexa. Oh, uh, Lester?
Lester, Alexa. Lester, Alexa. Well, I remember we had a band, a kazut band. I used to play piano, he played drum, and another boy called Albert played a kazut, was in the form of a trumpet.
You see? And we played many house parties, like two-cent house parties. Yeah. Nickel house parties like that. House be like that, be rolling. We played Saturday night fish fry.

All those kind of things, you know. When, the time when I played with those old timers, they used to take, they'd ask permission for my mother to take me on a job. Uh-huh. Then we'd make fifty cents that night, then they'd bring it home and they'd give my mother the fifty cents, and return me back to my, to my mother, you know. Yeah. Yeah, that's what they do. Yeah, I was too young to have money. Yeah. Yeah. Sometimes you make fifty cents a night. Get a good gig, you make a dollar. Mm-hmm.
